title: Kanchanaburi 3 Days 2 Nights: Waterfalls, History & Raft Stays
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Kanchanaburi itinerary covering Erawan Waterfall, the Death Railway and Tham Krasae, the Bridge over the River Kwai, and a night on a floating raft house — with opening hours, entry fees, and a real-world route through Thailand.
keywords: Kanchanaburi 3 day itinerary, Kanchanaburi trip, Erawan Waterfall, Death Railway, raft house Kanchanaburi
ogTitle: Kanchanaburi in 3 Days: Waterfalls, History & a Raft Stay
ogDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Kanchanaburi trip that balances nature, WWII history, and a night on a raft house along the River Kwai — with times and entry fees already checked for you.
intro: Kanchanaburi is only about a 2-hour drive from Bangkok, yet it packs in a huge range of things to do — a seven-tier waterfall, the historic Death Railway, and floating raft houses along the River Kwai. This 3-day, 2-night plan balances nature, history, and a relaxed night by the water, and it's sequenced so you keep moving forward instead of doubling back. Opening hours and entry fees are all checked and included.

blocks.html: Before we start, let's be honest: Kanchanaburi has more to see than you can fit into 3 days. For this plan we picked three core experiences — waterfalls, WWII history, and a night on a raft house on the River Kwai — the three things most first-time visitors want to tick off. If you have your own car you'll travel most comfortably, since the sights are spread out and public transport between districts isn't frequent.

From Bangkok to Kanchanaburi town is about 129 km — roughly a 2-hour drive if you're behind the wheel. Vans and buses mostly leave from the Southern Bus Terminal (Borommaratchachonnani) and take around 2–3 hours depending on traffic. Another option that's an experience in itself is riding the Death Railway from Thonburi Station, which runs straight past the Bridge over the River Kwai and the Tham Krasae cliffside section.

items: Self-drive — the most flexible, and ideal for this plan since you'll be heading out to Si Sawat and Sai Yok districts.
Van/bus — from the Southern Bus Terminal to Kanchanaburi town, fares run around a hundred-odd baht; from there rent a car or motorbike in town.
Death Railway — the Thonburi–Nam Tok line, with a morning departure around 07:36. Great if you want to soak up the railway hugging the cliffs.

blocks.title: Plan your nights smartly
blocks.html: For this itinerary, stay in town or along the River Kwai for the first night, then move out to a raft house around Sai Yok for the second night. That way you don't have to drive back into town every day, which saves a lot of time on the road.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Following the WWII trail through Kanchanaburi town

items.activity: Arrive in Kanchanaburi town and check in at a River Kwai riverside stay
items.note: If you arrive before check-in time, you can usually leave your bags at the resort first.
The burial site for WWII prisoners of war — a quiet, solemn place, free to enter, right in the center of town.

items.activity: War museum telling the story of the Death Railway
items.note: Get the historical background before seeing the real thing — it makes the sites far more meaningful.

items.activity: Lunch at a riverside restaurant on the River Kwai
items.note: The riverside strip near the bridge has plenty of Thai and river-fish restaurants to choose from.
Walk across the real steel bridge. Late afternoon light is softer and great for photos. Free to enter.

items.activity: Stroll the walking street / riverside market, dinner in town
items.note: Take it easy tonight and save your energy — tomorrow means a waterfall hike.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: The seven tiers of Erawan Waterfall, then off to a raft house

items.activity: Set off for Erawan Waterfall, Si Sawat district
items.note: About 65 km from town, roughly 1.5 hours. Go early — fewer people and clearer water.

items.activity: Hike Erawan Waterfall from tier 1 to as high as you feel up to
items.note: Entry is 60 THB for Thai adults, 30 THB for children. Open 08:00–16:00. Tiers 1–4 are an easy walk; tiers 5–7 get steeper and slippery, so wear shoes with good grip.

items.activity: Swim at your favorite tier, then head down for lunch near the parking area
items.note: There are restaurants and shops inside the park, but it's best to carry your own drinking water up.

items.activity: Continue to the Sai Yok side and check in at a floating raft house
items.note: Many raft houses along the River Kwai around Sai Yok require a boat to reach them — arrange a pickup by car or boat with the resort in advance.

items.activity: Relax on the raft and watch the sunset over the River Kwai
items.note: Some raft houses have spots for jumping in or kayaking. Raft room rates start around 3,000 THB per night and up, depending on the standard.

items.activity: Dinner at the resort's riverside dining room
items.note: There's no phone signal in some spots tonight — take it as a good chance to switch off.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Death Railway and Tham Krasae before heading home

items.activity: Breakfast on the raft, then check out without rushing
items.note: Make the most of the riverside atmosphere in the morning before you set off.
Located at km 64–65 on Route 323, free entry, open 09:00–16:00. There's a walking trail through the cutting that POWs dug by hand.

items.activity: Lunch, then on to Tham Krasae Station
items.note: This is the Death Railway section that runs along the cliffs beside the River Kwai. You can walk the wooden trestle for the views, no entry fee.

items.activity: Ride the Death Railway on the Tham Krasae–Saphan Kwae Yai stretch (if your timing lines up with the train)
items.note: Tickets are a few tens of baht for Thai passengers. Double-check the schedule on the spot, as times can change.

items.activity: Stop for souvenirs before heading back into town
items.note: Popular Kanchanaburi souvenirs include thong muan (crispy rolled wafers), traditional sweets, and dried fruit.
Allow extra time on Sunday evenings — traffic heading into Bangkok tends to back up.

blocks.text: Want to tweak the plan to your style?

items.name: Full history buff
items.blurb: Add Prasat Muang Sing (Khmer-era ruins, entry around 20 THB) and spend more time going through the museums in detail, with less time for swimming.

items.name: Nature lover
items.blurb: Swap the first day's museums for Sai Yok National Park or Srinakarin Dam, focusing on waterfalls and white-water rafting.

items.name: Riverside chill
items.blurb: Skip the higher waterfall tiers and add more time on the raft and at River Kwai cafés — ideal if you just want to relax.

blocks.title: Things to know before you go
blocks.html: Park entry fees and opening hours can change with the season, so it's worth checking the park's page before you travel. During the rainy season (Jun–Oct) the waterfalls are fuller and a lush green, but the trails get slippery; in the dry season the water is clearer but lower.

faq.q: Is 3 days and 2 nights enough for Kanchanaburi?
faq.a: It's enough for the core highlights — Erawan Waterfall, the Death Railway, the Bridge over the River Kwai, and one night on a raft house. But if you also want to reach Sangkhlaburi or Srinakarin Dam, you should allow 4 days or more.

faq.q: Do I need my own car for Kanchanaburi?
faq.a: Not strictly, but it's far more convenient, since the sights are spread across different districts and public transport between them isn't frequent. Without a car, rent a car or motorbike in town, or go with a day-tour package.

faq.q: How much is entry to Erawan Waterfall and what are the hours?
faq.a: It's 60 THB for Thai adults and 30 THB for children; for foreign visitors it's 300 THB for adults and 150 THB for children, plus around 30 THB for a car. It's open roughly 08:00–16:00. Go in the morning — fewer people and clearer water.

faq.q: About how much does a raft house on the River Kwai cost?
faq.a: Floating raft houses on the River Kwai start around 3,000 THB per night for mid-range options and run to several thousand baht for luxury floating villas. Many require a boat to reach them, so arrange a car or boat pickup with the resort in advance.

faq.q: What's the best time of year to visit Kanchanaburi?
faq.a: The late-rainy to early-cool season (Oct–Feb) has the nicest weather, with the waterfalls still full and a lush green. The hot season is good for cooling off in the water, though the waterfalls can run lower at times.
